'''Adiantum''' is a [[cipher]] composition for [[disk encryption]]. It uses a new cipher construction called HBSH (hash, block cipher, stream cipher, hash), specifically choosing [[UMAC (cryptography)#NH|NH]], 256-bit [[Advanced Encryption Standard]] (AES-256), (X)[[Salsa20#Reduced-round_ChaCha|ChaCha12]]/[[Salsa20#ChaCha_variant|ChaCha20]]{{efn|the paper also mentions the construction Adiantum-XChaCha20-AES and [[dm-crypt]] allows constructions like {{tt|xchacha20,aes-adiantum-plain64}}}}, [[Poly1305]] for the four elements.<ref name=TOSC18/> The version in Linux kernel preferentially uses XChaCha12, {{code|xchacha12,aes-adiantum}}.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Edge |first1=Jake |title=Adiantum: encryption for the low end |url=https://lwn.net/Articles/776721/ |website=LWN.net |date=16 January 2019}}</ref> 

It was designed in 2018 by Paul Crowley and Eric Biggers at [[Google]] specifically for low-powered mobile devices running [[Android Go]]. It has been included in the [[Linux kernel]] since version 5.0.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://lwn.net/Articles/776721/|title=Adiantum: encryption for the low end|date=January 6, 2019|website=LWN.net|publisher=Eklektix, Inc.|access-date=January 17, 2019}}</ref> The construct is designed to be "wide-block", where any change in the plaintext causes the entire ciphertext to be unrecognizably changed.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crowley |first1=Paul |last2=Biggers |first2=Eric  |title=Introducing Adiantum: Encryption for the Next Billion Users |url=https://security.googleblog.com/2019/02/introducing-adiantum-encryption-for.html |website=Google Online Security Blog |language=en}}</ref>

Adiantum is implemented in [[Android 10]] as an alternative cipher for device encryption, particularly on low-end devices lacking hardware-accelerated support for AES. (Adiantum only invokes AES once per plaintext.) The company stated that Adiantum ran five times faster than AES-256-XTS on [[ARM Cortex-A7]] CPUs.<ref name=TOSC18/> Google had previously exempted devices from mandatory device encryption if their specifications affected system performance if enabled. Due to the introduction of Adiantum, device encryption becomes mandatory on all Android devices beginning on Android 10.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.securityweek.com/google-improves-android-encryption-adiantum|title=Google Improves Android Encryption with Adiantum |website=SecurityWeek|date=8 February 2019 |access-date=2019-09-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2019/2/11/18220019/google-adiantum-storage-encryption-android-low-power-cheap-cost|title=Google wants to bring encryption to all with Adiantum|last=Porter|first=Jon|date=2019-02-11|website=The Verge|access-date=2019-09-05}}</ref>

'''HPolyC''' is an earlier variant which does not use NH.<ref name=TOSC18>{{cite journal |last1=Crowley |first1=Paul |last2=Biggers |first2=Eric |title=Adiantum: length-preserving encryption for entry-level processors |journal=IACR Transactions on Symmetric Cryptology |date=13 December 2018 |pages=39–61 |doi=10.13154/tosc.v2018.i4.39-61 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
